note: Generated by scripts/copy-sequences.mjs from sequences/*.json. Do not edit by hand.

sequences.name: Agency business development
sequences.description: For agencies and consultancies pitching a service. Leads with a result for a comparable client rather than a capabilities list, and offers something free that is actually free.
sequences.audience: Decision makers at companies matching the profile of your last three good clients — same size, same sector, same problem.

sequences.name: Alumni outreach
sequences.description: Reconnects with someone who shares your school or former employer, using the shared background as a natural reason to start a conversation.
sequences.audience: People who attended the same school or worked at the same former employer.

sequences.name: Community invite
sequences.description: Recruits people into a community, newsletter, or working group. Sells membership by naming who is already inside and what happens there, never by describing the community as "a place to connect".
sequences.audience: Practitioners who would make the community better by being in it — not a broad list. Quality of the room is the product.

sequences.name: Conference speaker follow-up
sequences.description: Follows up with someone after watching their conference talk, using a specific idea from the talk as the reason to connect.
sequences.audience: Conference speakers whose talk you watched and found relevant.

sequences.name: Connect then message
sequences.description: The shortest respectable sequence: an invite with a note, one message on acceptance, one polite close. Four touches total. Use it when you have volume and no time.
sequences.audience: A cold list where the value proposition does the work and personalisation beyond first name and company is not realistic.

sequences.name: Customer to case study
sequences.description: Asks a satisfied customer to share their experience publicly through a short, practical case study.
sequences.audience: Happy customers who have achieved a useful result with your product.

sequences.name: Dormant customer win-back
sequences.description: Reconnects with a former customer after a period of inactivity, starting with their current situation rather than immediately pitching.
sequences.audience: Former customers who stopped using the product around six months ago.

sequences.name: Executive search — confidential
sequences.description: Low-volume, high-discretion. Never names the client, never mentions a role in the invite note, and asks for a private channel before any detail moves. Built for searches where a leak is the failure mode.
sequences.audience: Senior operators — C-level, VP, founder-adjacent — on a confidential mandate. Small lists only, ten to thirty people.

sequences.name: Founder to founder
sequences.description: Peer-to-peer, no seller framing. Trades something useful before asking for anything, because the only currency that works founder to founder is being genuinely helpful first.
sequences.audience: Founders and co-founders at companies roughly your stage, in an adjacent market rather than a competing one.

sequences.name: Hiring manager intro
sequences.description: For a candidate approaching a hiring manager directly, bypassing the queue. Leads with proof of work rather than interest in the role, since the manager's problem is signal, not volume.
sequences.audience: Hiring managers at companies with a live role you can genuinely do. Ten to twenty targets, each one researched.

sequences.name: Investor introduction
sequences.description: Cold outreach to investors. Leads with a number, not a narrative, because that is the only thing that separates you from the other two hundred messages this week. Never asks for money in the first touch.
sequences.audience: Partners and principals at funds whose stage and thesis actually match where you are. Ten to forty names, researched individually.

sequences.name: Open-source maintainer to contributor
sequences.description: Reconnects with people who starred or forked a repository and opens a conversation about contributing.
sequences.audience: Developers who starred or forked your repository and may be interested in contributing.

sequences.name: Partnership outreach
sequences.description: For proposing an integration, a co-marketing push, or a referral arrangement. Leads with the overlap in customers, not with what you want, and asks for the right person early rather than pitching the wrong one.
sequences.audience: Partnerships, BD, and product leads at companies selling to the same buyer as you without competing for the same budget.

sequences.name: Podcast guest invite
sequences.description: Books guests for a show. Names the specific episode idea rather than asking "would you like to come on", because a concrete topic is far easier to say yes to than an open invitation.
sequences.audience: Practitioners with a specific, unusual, defensible opinion — not the professional-guest circuit.

sequences.name: Reactivation — dormant contact
sequences.description: For people you knew once and have not spoken to in years. Acknowledges the gap instead of pretending it isn't there, and asks about them before mentioning anything of your own.
sequences.audience: Lapsed connections, old colleagues, and prospects that went quiet more than a year ago. Where the person is already a first-degree connection the engine skips the invite step.

sequences.name: Recruiter — active candidate
sequences.description: For people who are visibly looking. Faster than the passive sequence, leads with the role, and asks for a call by the second message because their attention is finite and contested.
sequences.audience: Open-to-work badge, recent redundancy post, "currently exploring" headline, or applicants who went quiet.

sequences.name: Recruiter — passive candidate
sequences.description: For people who are not looking. Leads with respect for the fact that they are happy where they are, names the role only after acceptance, and exits gracefully. Slow on purpose.
sequences.audience: Employed, senior, not signalling any interest in moving. Long tenure, no open-to-work badge.

sequences.name: Referral ask
sequences.description: Asks someone to point you at the right person. Makes the ask small and specific — a name, not an introduction — because a name costs ten seconds and an introduction costs social capital.
sequences.audience: People adjacent to your buyer: former colleagues of theirs, advisors, or anyone who plainly knows the person you actually need.

sequences.name: SaaS trial nudge
sequences.description: For people who signed up, poked around, and stopped. Asks what got in the way rather than telling them what they missed. The most useful outcome of this sequence is often the answer, not the conversion.
sequences.audience: Trial signups that went inactive, imported as a CSV and resolved to LinkedIn profiles with a Research Pack.

sequences.name: Sales — competitor follower
sequences.description: For people following or engaging with a competitor. Never names the competitor and never rubbishes them — that reads as insecurity. Leads with the category problem instead.
sequences.audience: Lists built from a competitor's company followers or the engagers on a competitor's posts.

sequences.name: Sales — event attendee
sequences.description: Uses a shared event as the reason to exist. Works before the event ("are you going?") and after ("what did you make of it?"). Written for the after case, which converts better.
sequences.audience: Lists built from `event.attendees`, a conference badge scan, or a webinar registration export.

sequences.name: Sales — job change trigger
sequences.description: Fires on someone starting a new role. New leaders have budget, a mandate, and ninety days to show something. The fastest sequence here, because the window closes.
sequences.audience: Anyone whose profile shows a job change in the last 90 days — the `changed_job_90d` signal on a list or Research Pack.

sequences.name: Sales — post engager
sequences.description: For people who liked or commented on a post about your problem space. The trigger is fresh and specific, so this sequence moves faster and references the post directly in the first touch.
sequences.audience: Lists built from `post.engagers` on a post — yours or someone else's — that is about the problem you solve.

sequences.name: Speaker invite
sequences.description: Invites someone to speak at an event. States the date, the audience and the format in the first message, because a speaker's first three questions are always when, to whom, and how long.
sequences.audience: People whose work makes a talk obvious: they have shipped the thing your audience wants to hear about.

sequences.name: Warm connect
sequences.description: The default. Visit, follow, then invite with a short note two days later, so the invite lands on someone who has already seen your name. Two messages after acceptance, spaced wide.
sequences.audience: Anyone you have no relationship with yet and no specific trigger for. The safe starting template if you are unsure which to use.
